experiment: DFlash2 sidecar drafter on dense Qwen3.8-27B
context: first DFlash2 sidecar ever served on this card; ngl forced to 40 (vs 48 without sidecar) to make VRAM room for the drafter

finding: DFlash2's published acceptance claims are TRUE and if anything conservative: 0.737/0.519 with mean accepted length 3.93/3.08 — the best drafter acceptance ever measured on this card. But the NET decode (4.02/3.28 tok/s) loses to the embedded-MTP d2 baseline (4.63-5.3) because the sidecar's ~1.1 GB VRAM forces 8 main layers onto the CPU band (measured slope from our ngl sweeps: ~18% penalty).
conclusion: on 8 GB cards the DFlash2 family is VRAM-disqualified vs embedded MTP: acceptance quality cannot pay for the offload demotion. On 12 GB+ cards (3060 class, per the upstream cards' own target market) the drafter rides free and would win. Park again with this measured evidence.
family: andrew-paul Q2_K/Q3_K_M imatrix-calibrated variants untested (only andrew-paul's Q2_K saves ~400 MB vs Q8/Q4 — insufficient to recover 8 layers; no path to a win on 8 GB observed

finding: the Bonsai-specific DFlash2 sidecar (ProCreations/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-DFlash2, Q8_0 1.915 GB, sha 9dd11c8a…, downloaded+verified) also cannot fit this card: OOM at main ngl 60 AND ngl 54 (draft buffer 1950.71 MiB is the failing alloc each time); fitting it would need main ngl ~44 + partially-CPU drafting, which defeats a block-diffusion drafter. ALSO: DFlash2's new tensor layout (58 tensors + selector/convolution) is rejected by our bonsai2 fork ('expected 81, got 58') and DFlash-v1 loaders — it requires ProCreations' patched runtime (prism-dflash2 source; built successfully here for sm75; the load failure is pure VRAM, not format).
runtime_note: prism-dflash2 source (= newer base with PTQ1_0 merged upstream + DFlash2 support) builds clean for sm75 — kept at ~/models/bonsai-dflash2/llama/ as the future runtime for ANY DFlash2 sidecar
conclusion: both DFlash2 configurations that exist today are VRAM-disqualified on 8 GB. Retry trigger: a Q2_K/Q4_K-class sidecar (~500-700 MB) for the 27B or Bonsai families — at that size the Bonsai pairing (bare main 5.54 GB + sidecar in spare room at ngl 60) becomes viable and is the highest-upside drafter test remaining for this card
